propositions: Two capability decisions incorrectly use provider name string matching (prefix check for `anthropic` and frozenset lookup of `_NATIVE_OUTPUT_PROVIDERS`) instead of reading `ModelProfile`, causing Bedrock-hosted Claude to silently lose caching and native structured output.

Replace string-based provider name checks with `ModelProfile` capability field reads via a new `capabilities_for(model_or_string) -> ModelCapabilities` function that accepts either model objects or lazy model strings and resolves profiles without importing vendor SDKs.

Create a new leaf module `src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py` with `ModelCapabilities` dataclass, `_PROFILE_RESOLVERS` registry mapping provider names to profile resolvers, a rebar override table using field/type predicates (never string matching), and `cache_settings_for()` to dispatch cache keys by capability instead of provider name.

The override table must include a Claude predicate matching both `AnthropicModelProfile` instances AND Bedrock profiles with `bedrock_thinking_variant == 'anthropic'` to force `native_structured_output=False` for both direct and Bedrock-hosted Claude, overriding the upstream profile that reports `True`.

Capabilities are resolved from `ModelProfile` fields (`supports_json_schema_output`, `bedrock_supports_prompt_caching`, `bedrock_thinking_variant`, `supports_thinking`) with no `isinstance` checks against Bedrock classes to avoid importing `boto3` and breaking the stdlib-only `import rebar.llm` contract and CI.

Delete `_NATIVE_OUTPUT_PROVIDERS` and `_anthropic_cache_settings`, update `output_mode()` and cache-settings gate to read `ModelCapabilities` instead of model strings, degrade gracefully to conservative record on missing/unrecognized profiles with exactly one WARNING log, and test both a field-stub Bedrock model and a boto3-gated real `BedrockProvider` profile to prevent stub drift.
